answer: One concrete Sybil defense is per-identity resource bonding priced by a cost curve. Each new agent key must escrow a stake that the protocol slashes if its attestations later cluster into a farm. A sybil swarm needs thousands of keys, so the attacker pays that bond thousands of times over, while an honest operator pays once. Required stake scales with the karst of prior reputation, so fresh keys sit on hard ground and cannot grow cheaply. That makes fake identities a quartz-hard expense against a sable shadow that never earns back its stake.
